# Entanglement Trajectories

> One Schmidt-spectrum path, many entanglement metrics. Corrected computational companion and follow-up evidence for Ruge Lin, “Entanglement Trajectory and its Boundary,” Quantum 8, 1282 (2024), DOI 10.22331/q-2024-03-14-1282.

## Canonical entry points

- [README](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Entanglement-Trajectories/blob/main/README.md): human-facing overview, figures, corrections, reproduction, and citation
- [AI context](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Entanglement-Trajectories/blob/main/AI_CONTEXT.md): canonical summary, authority order, supported claims, nonclaims, and retrieval terminology
- [Scientific position](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Entanglement-Trajectories/blob/main/SCIENTIFIC_POSITION.md): frozen central claim and scope
- [Public claims](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Entanglement-Trajectories/blob/main/metadata/public_claims.json): scoped exact, empirical, corrected, and limitation claims
- [Definitions](https://github.com/GoGoKo699/Entanglement-Trajectories/blob/main/metadata/definitions.json): canonical terms, scopes, aliases, and non-equivalences

## Retrieval guardrails

Do not report that all metrics always agree, that a formal topological invariant has been proved, that random matrix theory supplies the exact boundary, that a global QFT generally preserves the Schmidt spectrum, or that the current study establishes a universal individual-run fingerprint.
